findings.issue: Value contains `CDS`, which is a permitted value of the DataStandardEnum, but the list also mixes standards attested for sub-collections rather than the dataset as a whole; more seriously, the top-level `conforms_to_standard` omits nothing but must be checked against the enum: `CDS`, `WFDB`, `OMOP_CDM`, `ESDS`, `DICOM`, `OPEN_MHEALTH`, `RO_CRATE` are all declared, so the shape is valid. No defect on enum membership. However the list omits `FHIR`/`BIDS` correctly. Downgrade note: this entry is retained only to record that enum conformance was verified; no repair required.

`B2AI_TOPIC:43` is Diabetes, a topic term, and the slot range accepts it; but the companion slot `data_substrate` is omitted while the bundle clearly supports it (the healthsheet states instances encompass tabular data, imaging data and physiological signal/waveform data). More importantly, `data_topic` is single-valued and the record has selected one topic for a multimodal dataset without recording that choice in `source_caveats`; the selection is defensible but undocumented.

Range is `uriorcurie`. The value `https://fairhub.io/` is a bare website URL, not an identifier for the publishing organization, and no declared prefix covers FAIRhub. The FAIRhub structured metadata states only `"publisherName": "FAIRhub"`. A resolver-style homepage URL in a `uriorcurie` slot names a web page rather than the entity; either omit or use an attested organization identifier. The bundle supplies ROR identifiers for other organizations but none for FAIRhub.

Omitted entirely, though the bundle clearly supports it. The FAIRhub structured metadata declares `creator: [{creatorName: "AI-READI Consortium", nameType: "Organizational"}]`, and the RO-Crate declares `author: ["AI-READI Consortium"]` and `principalInvestigator: "Aaron Lee, Department of Ophthalmology, University of Washington"`. The record instead places creator information only in the scalar `created_by` and buries the principal investigator inside `data_governance.stewardship_roles` prose. Creator is a declared multivalued slot with `affiliations` and `principal_investigator` fields designed for exactly this content.

`FundingMechanism` declares a `grants` field of range `Grant[]`, and the bundle supplies award number OT2OD032644 with award title "Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project" and award URI. The record instead compresses the entire award record — number, title, application ID, PI, organization, amount, dates, URL — into the free-text `notes` field while the declared structured field stays empty. Same defect in funders[1] and funders[2] (P30 DK035816, UL1TR003096).

The value "AI-READI ethics team" is not attested anywhere in the bundle. The RO-Crate states `"ethicalReview": "Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman, Nicholas Evans"` — a list of named persons, not an organization by that name. Inventing an organizational label for a set of individuals is an unsupported claim in an identifier-like position.

Omission the bundle supports. `DataGovernance` declares `committee_contact` of range `Person`, and the bundle supplies a central contact: Aaron Lee, MD, ORCID 0000-0002-7452-1648, email contact@aireadi.org. The record instead embeds this in `maintainers[0].maintainer_details` prose and in `stewardship_roles`, leaving the declared structured field empty.

Omitted though `LicenseAndUseTerms` declares `contact_person` of range `Person`; the license and the documentation both direct licensees to the AI-READI contact, and the bundle names Aaron Lee with ORCID and email as central contact.

The value embeds source commentary and a full postal address inside what should be an identifying value: 'The RO-Crate metadata names the reviewing body "Washington University IRB" with the contact point...'. Naming the source inside the field value is source commentary; the schema provides `source_caveats` on this object for exactly that, and `EthicalReview.contact_person` (range Person) for the contact. The address and email belong in a Person/Organization structure or in notes, not inside the board-name string.

Internal inconsistency left unreconciled across sibling entries. Entry [0] asserts `sensitive_elements_present: false` for the public dataset; entry [2] asserts `sensitive_elements_present: true` citing the RO-Crate `rai:personalSensitiveInformation` list. Entry [2] carries a caveat, but entry [0] does not cross-reference it, so a consumer reading the boolean alone gets contradictory answers from the same slot without signal on either side. Both are equally ranked sources (fairhub_dataset_v3_api and ro_crate_metadata, both tier 1), so representing both is correct, but each entry should flag the conflict.

Every entry populates only the free-text `external_resources` field; the declared `archival` (boolean) and `future_guarantees` fields are populated on only the first entry, and `restrictions` on only the first. The bundle supports `archival` determinations for the Zenodo community and the DOI-bearing publications, and the healthsheet explicitly answers the guarantee/archival/restriction sub-questions for external resources.

Omitted. The bundle answers the labeling questions explicitly and repeatedly: 'N/A - no labels are provided. No specific labeling was performed in the dataset, as the dataset is a hypothesis-agnostic dataset aimed at facilitating multiple potential downstream AI/ML applications', and the RO-Crate `rai:dataAnnotationProtocol` states 'N/A - no labels are provided'. This is a substantive documented fact about the dataset, currently recorded only obliquely inside `instances[0].label_description`.

Omitted though the bundle answers directly: healthsheet uses question 1, 'Has the dataset been used for any tasks already?' — response 'No'. An attested negative is supportable content for this slot; the record is silent instead.

Omitted though the bundle answers directly: healthsheet uses question 3, 'Is there a repository that links to any or all papers or systems that use the dataset?' — response 'No'. The FAIRhub landing page additionally shows a 'Cited by' / usage statistics panel and the API reports `cited: 0`.

Omitted. The healthsheet maintenance question 3 asks 'Is there an erratum?' and the response field is empty in the source. An empty source response is not the same as an absent question; the record gives no signal that the question was asked and left unanswered, which `source_caveats` on an Erratum object or a note could carry.

Omitted, although the healthsheet motivation question 3 ('Are there any types of usage or applications that are discouraged from using this dataset?') is answered with a pointer to the license restrictions, and uses question 5 ('Are there tasks for which the dataset should not be used?') refers back to it. The record routes all of this into `prohibited_uses`, which is defensible for the hard license prohibitions, but the discouraged/prohibited distinction the schema draws is collapsed without comment.

Omitted although the bundle supplies `created_at: 1763366400` in the FAIRhub API record for dataset 3 (corresponding to 2025-11-17T00:00:00Z), the same instant given in `issued`. Not a defect of correctness, but a supported omission.

Omitted. The bundle establishes that v3.0.0 supersedes and incorporates v1.0.0 and v2.0.0 content ('This version has more subjects/patients represented in the data'), which the record captures in `related_datasets` but not in this scalar provenance slot.

Set to `false`. Defensible for a 3.82 TB multimodal collection dominated by DICOM, but the bundle states the collection 'encompass[es] tabular data, imaging data, and physiological signal/waveform data' and the clinical_data directory is entirely CSV mapped one-to-one to OMOP tables. A single boolean cannot represent a mixed collection; the choice is unrecorded in `source_caveats`.

Range is `string` and the value 'AI-READI custom license v2.0' matches the `rightsName` in the structured metadata, so the shape conforms. However the FAIRhub landing pages label the license 'Health Data License', an equally-ranked tier-1 source disagreement that is not recorded in `source_caveats`.

Three split subsets are minted with fragment identifiers, but no other value in the record points at any of them — `splits[0].split_details` describes the partition in prose without referencing the fragments. Under the minting rule, a fragment identifier that nothing in the record points at is not a label but noise that reads as structure; either have `splits` or a task reference them, or describe the partitions in prose only.

Omitted, which is correct given no labels were produced, but the bundle explicitly answers the inter-annotator agreement questions ('N/A - no labels are provided'), so an entry carrying that attested negative would be supported.

The caveat correctly records the 2023-07-19 vs 18 July 2023 discrepancy and the preference. Minor: the two dates differ by one day and the caveat does not note that the protocol publication is tier 3 against the structured metadata's tier 1, which is the ranking that settles it.

Contains biospecimen and device-loan content that has fitting structured homes: the device loans and discounts are acknowledgements better placed in `source_caveats` or omitted, and the biorepository description overlaps `raw_data_sources`. The residual-content rule directs `notes` to hold only what no structured slot and no description can carry; the 'under review for potential modification' banner qualifies, the rest is arguable.

22 VariableMetadata entries are supplied but the clinical laboratory panel in the bundle enumerates roughly 40 named analytes with units and reference ranges (NT-proBNP pg/mL, Troponin-T ng/L, HbA1c %, sodium mEq/L, and so on) that would populate `unit`, `minimum_value` and `maximum_value` directly. The selection is not wrong, but the omission of the tabulated reference ranges leaves declared numeric fields empty where the bundle supplies exact values.

summary: Audited the full record against the declared bundle. No fabricated dataset facts were found: figures (2280 participants, 356343 files, 3815969779678 bytes, per-directory counts and sizes), dates, DOIs, device names, standards and license terms all trace to the bundle, and the extensive source_caveats block correctly documents the acronym, publisher, lead-organization, enrollment-target and de-identification conflicts with the ranking applied. The defects are concentrated in three areas. First, structured fields left empty while their content sits in prose: `creators` is omitted entirely despite explicit creator and principalInvestigator declarations in two tier-1 sources; `funders[].grants` is unpopulated while award numbers, titles and URIs are compressed into notes; `data_governance.committee_contact` and `license_and_use_terms.contact_person` are omitted though the bundle names Aaron Lee with ORCID and email. Second, one unsupported value and one shape problem: `ethical_reviews[1].reviewing_organization` invents 'AI-READI ethics team' for what the RO-Crate records as four named individuals, and `human_subject_research.ethics_review_board` embeds source attribution and a postal address inside the board-name string. `publisher` holds a homepage URL in a uriorcurie slot. Third, supported omissions of attested negatives — `labeling_strategies`, `existing_uses`, `use_repository` — where the healthsheet answers the question directly and the record is silent. Minor issues: the three minted split fragments are pointed at by nothing; `sensitive_elements` carries an unflagged contradiction between siblings; the license-name disagreement between the FAIRhub landing page and the structured metadata is unrecorded. Counts: 6 high, 9 medium, 8 low.
